item.title: Phil Collins Says ‘People Were Coming to Say Goodbye’ Amidst Alcoholism Battle
item.description:
[Energizing music fades out]
Host: Welcome to this week's music update. Today, we're talking about the legendary Phil Collins. The 75-year-old music icon has been open about his recent struggles with alcoholism in a candid interview with The Sunday Times.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: Collins shared that he was hospitalized in Switzerland in April 2024 after a relapse with alcohol. His condition was so severe that his manager summoned his five children to say their goodbyes. Collins revealed that his kidneys were failing, and his organs were shutting down. Fortunately, he pulled through, and it's been a wake-up call for him.
[Short music transition]
Host: Collins has been open about his struggles with alcoholism before, even discussing it in his 2016 memoir Not Dead Yet. He'd been sober for a while, thanks to medication, but unfortunately, he started drinking again. He can't pinpoint exactly when, but it got to the point where he'd start his day with a glass of wine.
[Soft music continues]
Host: After a series of hospital visits, including a seven-month stay in intensive care, Collins says he's lucky to be alive and hasn't had a drink since. On a more positive note, he's also made amends with Paul McCartney, after a previous rift. Collins had said that McCartney treated him condescendingly, but the two have since made up, thanks in part to an upcoming charity auction.
[Music transitions to a more uplifting tone]
Host: And some exciting news for Phil Collins fans - he'll be inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a solo act in November, alongside other music legends like Billy Idol and Iron Maiden. We're wishing Phil all the best on his road to recovery and looking forward to celebrating his incredible contributions to music.
[Music and host continue for another 5 seconds before fading out]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in!
